v.q: Which Java release introduced lambdas and the Stream API?
v.w: Java 8 (2014) added lambdas, streams, `Optional`, default methods and the new date-time API.

v.q: Which feature does NOT come from Java 8?
v.w: Records arrived in Java 16. Lambdas, streams and the date and time API are Java 8.

v.q: Which feature arrived in Java 9 and reshaped how large applications are packaged?
v.w: Java 9 added modules with `module-info.java`. Many projects still run on the classpath.

v.q: Which feature is NOT a Java 9 change?
v.w: Virtual threads were finalised in Java 21.

v.q: What does `var` do in `var list = new ArrayList<String>();` (Java 10)?
o: The compiler infers the type; the variable stays statically typed
The variable becomes dynamically typed at run time
The variable can hold any other type later on
The variable is made automatically final
v.w: `var` is only for local variables with an initialiser. It is not a keyword for fields or method parameters.

v.q: Which statement about var is NOT true?
o: It makes the variable dynamically typed
It infers the type from the initialiser
It is allowed for local variables
The type is fixed at compile time
v.w: var is only type inference. The compiler fixes the type.

v.q: Which of these is a long-term support (LTS) release?
v.w: LTS releases are 8, 11, 17, 21 and 25. Between them are six-month feature releases. Spring Boot 3 requires Java 17 or later.

v.q: Which is NOT an LTS release?
v.w: Long-term support releases are 8, 11, 17 and 21. Releases in between are supported only until the next one.

o: A concise immutable data carrier with generated accessors and `equals`
A class that logs every method call it receives
A database row that only Hibernate can map
A thread-safe list implementation for queues
v.w: Records suit DTOs and value objects. Their fields are final and they cannot extend another class.

v.q: What does a record generate automatically?
o: A database table and its mapping
A REST endpoint for each field
v.w: A record declares its components and the compiler writes the boilerplate.

v.q: What problem do virtual threads (Java 21) mainly address?
o: Handling very many blocking tasks without one OS thread each
Speeding up CPU-heavy number crunching on all cores
Replacing the garbage collector with a new one
v.w: Virtual threads are scheduled by the JVM on a few carrier threads. Blocking I/O parks them cheaply. CPU-bound work gains nothing.

v.q: Which kind of workload gains most from virtual threads?
v.w: A virtual thread parks while waiting, so a few carrier threads serve many blocked tasks.

v.q: What do sealed classes (Java 17) let you do?
o: Restrict which classes may extend or implement a type
Prevent any class from ever being instantiated
Encrypt the class files on disk
Make every field of the class private
v.w: `sealed ... permits A, B` gives a closed hierarchy. Together with pattern matching in `switch`, the compiler can check exhaustiveness.

v.q: Which class declaration uses Java 17 sealed types correctly?
o: sealed interface Shape permits Circle, Square
v.w: sealed with permits lists the allowed subtypes, so a switch over them can be exhaustive.

v.q: Which Java 15+ feature makes multi-line strings, such as embedded JSON or SQL, easier to write?
o: Text blocks written with triple quotes
v.w: Text blocks (`""" ... """`) remove most escaping and keep indentation sensible.

v.q: Which Java feature gives a switch that returns a value with arrow labels?
v.w: Switch expressions (Java 14) yield a value, need no break and can be exhaustive.
